approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs, breeds from score quantiles, constructs fresh offspring by crossover and atom/bond edits, and retains high-scoring survivors. Before each batch it fits two session-local predictors to the complete accepted archive: a count-fingerprint Gaussian process, and a fixed boosted-tree regressor of raw score differences on every ordered molecular pair. The active location for each new candidate is the best observed molecule's score plus the predicted difference from that one reference. The original GP still supplies correlated residual draws and, after three non-improving batches, the forty-candidate eligibility screen. Ten distinct candidates are bought sequentially, and only their real accepted scores update the search.
approach.novelty: Replace the privileged best-molecule reference with the equal-weight average of predictions anchored at every accepted molecule. This changes reference support at inference while keeping the learned directional difference model, residual draws and eligibility screen. It tests whether reference-dependent errors can be reduced in a way that changes paid choices, rather than only shifting every prediction by the same amount. No completed sibling has tried this on the Parent; the separately scheduled sibling repairs opposite-direction consistency while retaining one reference. This experiment keeps the raw directional predictions and does not combine those two corrections.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-7e9f57600099 makes every active location depend on the earliest accepted maximum-score reference despite an exposed, refuted predictive claim. Its full Analyze report nodes/n-7e9f57600099/analysis.json records 435 correct fits, 4350 prospective paid joins, 435 changed sets and 2425 actual-only identities, yet all-paid raw-location MSE is 0.009326712412663193 versus same-state original-GP 0.005240750463529221, worse in all 15 cells. The 3892 below-incumbent purchases dominate that error; pool self/swap absolute defects are 0.016086661654860494/0.022578409367158204. These defects are measured limitations, not established causes of endpoint loss. Search Policy's policy/scratch/search_policy-98a37040179e/reference-geometry-summary.json and its 15 source audits show nonzero double-centered accepted reference interactions in all 435 fits, but per-cell interaction-to-total squared-magnitude fractions are only 0.0005297031674573093 to 0.004094873477951108. The complete read-only reproduction at policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/improve/geometry-recheck-summary.json agrees exactly; its individual audit-seed-N-task.json files identify every original log/trajectory and hash. This is in-sample evidence that exact additivity does not hold, not a measurement of future all-reference predictions or a promise of changed ordering. The single-reference error and observed reference dependence justify this specific support intervention. Mean 0.5248434366619207 and finalized task_safe=false remain separate from the original frozen lock-mismatched comparison to n-cf8d309c06de: paired_complete=false, matched_seeds=[], paired_mean_delta=null. Current Curate lesson h-19f2d01cf07af401 in the frozen catalog preserves that boundary. The exposed screen control n-c501ea219a1c supports a conditional retained-screen result on its original GP host, not transfer to this cardinal host; its catalog applicability limitation remains. Parent chemistry in nodes/n-7e9f57600099/molecular.json describes local family concentration and both size tails without authorizing a generator or reward change.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen B1/B3 planning review and its recorded queries; the PADRE primary PDF was reopened and its inference equations verified during PLAN, with provenance at policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/improve/literature-verification.json. Internal evidence is the Parent's complete refuted prediction plus small nonzero accepted reference interactions, reproduced from every original Search cell. Adopt only uniform raw-direction reference aggregation. Deliberately omit the other portfolio operation, TNNR simultaneous antisymmetrization, and any learned weights, nearest-reference selection, feature change, learner replacement, uncertainty pricing or active candidate edges. No official code, source dataset, pretrained model or dependency is introduced. The additive-model derivation is a discriminating limitation: an offset can improve MSE without changing ordering. The full new same-paid prediction and actual choice exposure remain untested until this separate Child runs; the original scientific verdict and comparator incompleteness remain unchanged.

hypothesis: At each unchanged pre-suggestion refit, freeze all n chronological real accepted records L={(c_i,y_i)} used by the existing raw-difference regressor D(i,x) approximately equal to y_x-y_i. Replace only the active location mu_b(x)=y_b+D(b,x) by mu_all(x)=(1/n)*sum_{i in L}(y_i+D(i,x)), with all references contributing once and equally. Keep raw directional D and its measured diagonal, antisymmetry and cycle defects; do not retrain differently or symmetrize. Retain the original GP residual R and original-GP-mean eligibility so active purchase values become mu_all(x)+R. The mechanism removes privileged-reference support and may reduce reference-specific error. If D(i,x)=u(i)+v(x), the location difference is a candidate-constant offset and cannot improve ideal ordering; candidate-dependent displacement, strict rank/choice changes and real paid exposure must be measured independently of calibration. The direct prediction is strictly lower complete same-paid raw-score MSE than the passive unchanged mu_b on actual Child histories after correct nonconstant exposure and changed paid identities. Endpoint gain is a separate conditional prediction.

finding_summary.headline: All-reference prediction changed purchases and lowered full-stream error, with a conditional endpoint gain.
finding_summary.insights:
The reference-support intervention reached paid choices, with nonconstant changes in all 435 pools and 268222 strict rank reversals within eligible sets. The uniform labeled-reference mean borrowed from PADRE operated, while the source's feature-difference block, random-forest model and reference-dispersion uncertainty were deliberately absent. Thus this finding concerns the frozen hybrid, not the full published method. On the realized purchases, the common-offset part changes MSE by -0.000891157904 and the remaining candidate-varying part by 0.000357255091; this algebraic separation does not identify how changed choices relate to the endpoint gain. The raw-error gain is dominated by common-offset calibration: the candidate-varying part gives back some of that reduction. Error also worsened on the 353 purchases above the announcement incumbent, even though it improved on the 3,927 below it. This supports the finite selected-stream correction while leaving better discovery of improving candidates, reliable benefit and causal mediation open. The original difference-model-versus-GP prediction remains refuted. The new location still predicts and orders purchased outcomes worse than the passive GP, and raw self, swap and cycle defects remain. A different surrogate or ranking model is the relevant kind of method for that remaining prediction limitation; this experiment establishes no replacement benefit.

The molecular assessment also shows a proposal limitation that the inference change did not remove. The large-molecule tail shrank from 837 to 607 purchases with at least 50 heavy atoms, yet 519 of the Child cases came from one task. Overall there were 1,969 typed and 1,240 generic scaffolds, but two leading task-level sets occupied only four and seven generic scaffolds. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity remained high, increasing from 0.743529 to 0.749127. That is local family concentration alongside broad aggregate variety, not universal scaffold collapse. Coherent core, linker or ring proposal operators are the type of change that could address that limitation; their score benefit remains unmeasured. Unusual bond environments and missing stereochemical states further limit chemical interpretation. Neither the chemistry nor the downstream feedback associations establish mediation, authorize a new intervention, or decide whether the approach should continue.
finding_summary.results: All 435 scheduled fits and 4,350 purchased prediction–label joins completed correctly. Every pool had a candidate-varying location change; 364 of 435 purchase sets changed and 784 actual purchases were absent from the passive incumbent-based set. The complete-stream mean squared error fell from 0.00918329074 to 0.00864938792, so the registered prediction passed under its strict rule. Error improved in 11 task/seed cells and worsened in 4; every cell remains in that result. The passive GP still had error 0.00546584168 on these same purchases. Paid ordering accuracy, counting prediction ties as half correct, was 64.76% for the new location, 63.86% for the incumbent location and 69.74% for the GP. All 4,200 nonterminal purchases entered the next fit; 150 final-batch purchases had no later fit opportunity. The final macro score increased from 0.524843 to 0.547030, a certified paired gain of 0.022187, exceeding the separate +0.002 code-Parent target. Ten endpoint cells improved and five declined. Most net gain came from sitagliptin and zaleplon objectives, while the mean median-similarity and decoration-hopping scores declined; seed dispersion increased from 0.008692 to 0.024079. This comparison does not satisfy the formal Anchor target of 0.609030 because that criterion requires the Anchor itself as code Parent and comparator. No Child task-safety flag or margin was supplied.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analogues and polyamine cages, with uneven size control, unusual bond environments and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 15 original Child and 15 published code-Parent Search trajectories were read for frozen seeds 0/1/2. Each node contributes 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases and 150 supplied initial observations; chemistry totals and similarities below exclude initials. These are purchased, scored molecules, not every generated or unpurchased pool member. No issued trajectory is missing and no task is omitted. The output is overwhelmingly cyclic and aromatic: digest ring-closure rates span 0.9943–1.0 and aromatic-presence rates 0.9839–1.0. It contains aromatic carboxamides, extended heteroaryl carbonyl systems, aryl-substituted cyclic polyamines, condensed aza-aromatic/lactam systems and fluorinated bridged carbonyl heterocycles. These recognizable motifs coexist with heteroatom–halogen bonds, peroxide links, cyclic cumulated bonds and complicated ring junctions; synthetic plausibility is questionable overall, not experimentally disproved. The drug-likeness chip is a structural judgment, not an ADME or usefulness result. Child heavy-atom median/range are 33 and 1–120; Parent values are 32 and 2–120. Retaining both historical source-defined size conventions, Child counts at <=5, <=6, >=50 and >50 heavy atoms are 8, 8, 607 and 597, versus 4, 4, 837 and 828 in the Parent. The upper tail remains concentrated: 519 Child purchases in one covered task have >=50 atoms. Typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1,969/1,240 versus 2,038/1,366, including the empty acyclic scaffold; distinct strings do not equal independent chemotypes. Radius-2 chirality-aware 2,048-count Morgan dot-product Tanimoto, using unordered pairs only within each task/seed session, averages 0.652628 for Child and 0.642373 for Parent. Excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments gives 0.654981 and 0.643513. Within actual ten-purchase batches the corresponding values are 0.746456/0.742229, or 0.749127/0.743529 after fragment exclusion. These pair-count-weighted descriptions never compare molecules across independent sessions. Broad aggregate topology therefore coexists with similar local analogues; diversity is not universally collapsed. All 4,350 Child purchases lack formal charges, assigned tetrahedral configurations and specified double-bond geometry. RDKit identifies 6,666 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,672 molecules. Neutral depiction does not establish solution protonation state. The inherited audit field named cumulene uses the generic pattern [*]=[*]=[*], which also matches sulfonyl sulfur: the supplemental bond audit separates 276 Child molecules with carbon-centred matches from 341 with sulfur-centred matches. Ordinary sulfonyl matches are not counted as chemical liabilities merely because this generic flag fires. The exact issued Child–code-Parent comparison is complete for both nodes and paired on seeds 0/1/2, without profile-mismatched seeds. The code Parent is n-7e9f57600099; its older comparison to another ancestor was unpaired and is not this comparison. Chemistry contrasts here do not identify component effects, activation, score causation or selection. Top-87 descriptions mean the highest supplied scores among 870 optimizer purchases per task with fixed seed/evaluation ties; this descriptive subset can concentrate in one seed and is not independent replication. Methods, all per-cell records and source-defined boundaries are in policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and its named audits; bond semantics are in policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/bond-context-audit.json. Original-to-copy authority is in policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/original-input-mapping.json. Current completeness comes from policy/requests/r0072-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-075576f926f95339.json#context.comparison; historical chemistry context is nodes/n-7e9f57600099/molecular.json. Per-task sources below include every underlying trajectory alongside the audits.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 purchases have median 25 heavy atoms, range 3–51, and median three perceived rings. The leading families are substituted indole-like carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings, with methoxy/alkyl groups and frequent N-halogen substitutions. Seed 1 also reaches a benzene-fused four-membered unsaturated carbocycle bearing an N-fluoro carboxamide. All three seed leaders remain compact, at 25, 23 and 25 heavy atoms. The Parent also concentrated on this aromatic amide neighborhood: its median was 26 atoms, and the Child top-87 set has 13 typed/four generic scaffolds versus five/two in the Parent. These are recognizable organic motifs, but many exact analogues have unusual bond environments. liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 371 purchases and 69 of the top-87 set. The seed-0 leader also has a bromomethyl substituent and an N–N connection; the seed-2 leader has both amide N–F and ring N–Cl.
The seed-1 leader contains a fused four-membered unsaturated ring. Its accepted graph and score do not demonstrate a feasible conformation or synthesis.
missing_features: Distinct compact core alternatives are only sparsely represented among the leading analogues: four generic scaffold topologies in the top-87 set. The rows do not identify a required missing target-specific functional group.

Conventional N-substitution is not reliably retained around the successful amide motif: all three seed leaders contain an N-halogen bond, so these trajectories do not demonstrate equally successful ordinary amide counterparts.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial indole carboxamide at seed 0/evaluation 9 scored 0.3051048083696145. Child seed leaders at evaluations 300, 266 and 258 score 0.46092619585962435, 0.45975204214862936 and 0.4519753205796759. The top-87 set spans 22–26 heavy atoms and retains three rings throughout. At the low end, dimethyl ether scores 3.563993999218106e-16 and a 51-atom, seven-aromatic-ring concatenation scores 5.631227773275544e-23. The visible association is retention of compact aromatic/carboxamide organization with selective decoration; neither fragmentation nor simple aromatic enlargement is sufficient. N-halogen-bearing leaders are observed, but these comparisons do not isolate a benefit of the N-halogen bond.

per_task.generated_character: The purchases span 11–120 heavy atoms, with median 54 atoms and five perceived rings. Aromatic N/O heterocycles, ring carbonyls, aryl/heteroaryl links and halogenated alkyl/ether substituents dominate. Seed-1 leaders are comparatively compact four-ring heteroaryl systems; seed 0 retains an imine/anilino-linked carbonyl-rich heterocycle, while seed 2 builds much larger repeated aromatic/carbonyl assemblies. The Child top-87 set is 32–46 atoms, whereas the Parent counterpart spans 68–120. This is uneven size control, not absence of the ability to form compact heterocycles. The 83-atom seed-2 leader includes a perceived four-membered cycle built from aromatic atoms, nine-membered cycles and unspecified polyene geometry. Aromatic atom flags do not make every bond or that small cycle aromatic. Repetition and ring perception do not establish synthetic accessibility.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed leaders are 38 atoms/0.599535997605149, 36 atoms/0.6211616722160562 and 83 atoms/0.6006121905775885. A small fluorinated methoxy benzonitrile scores 0.5056982554571754; a smaller N-methoxy fused imide-like heterocycle scores 0.5164082369349414. Thus higher values associate with elaborated, linked heteroaryl/carbonyl organization, but size alone is not monotonic: the 36-atom family exceeds the much larger seed-2 leader. Its seven-ring median is heavily influenced by the seed-1 family; the other seed leaders do not establish a universal advantage of additional fusion.

Compact, fluorinated carbonyl/N-heterocycle systems dominate late output, but ring fusion and bridging are extensive. Seed 0 builds an eight-ring sulfur-bridged imino/lactam/lactone framework; seed 1 a partly aromatic fused imide-like framework with phenol and a fluorinated thiol-bearing carbon; seed 2 a fused imino carbonyl core linked to an unsaturated N-heterocycle with O–Cl. liabilities: The leading seed-2 molecule has a covalent O–Cl bond and a perceived four-membered ring; leading seed-1 analogues contain thiol-bearing fluorinated carbon centers, and other high-score analogues have N–F.

Seed-0 eight-ring cages and seed-2 imino/unsaturated heterocycles combine several stereochemical and ring-junction constraints without conformer or synthesis evidence. The smaller sizes do not by themselves settle plausibility.
missing_features: All top-87 structures have unassigned tetrahedral centers, while none has an assigned configuration. The three leaders have three, three and five unassigned centers respectively.

Only eleven typed/seven generic scaffolds occur in the top-87 set, so varied compact cores with conventional substituent chemistry remain thinly represented. No required missing target-specific group can be inferred from the displayed scalar scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three leaders score 0.35059847823951884, 0.5071850752852776 and 0.5761152248528798. A 62-atom aromatic imide/amide concatenation scores 3.2416258040348776e-69; similarly large conjugates are poor in the other seeds. The Child top-87 set has 25–31 atoms and median 28, versus a 43-atom median among the bottom-87 set. The visible gradient favors compact, reorganized carbonyl/N-heterocyclic arrangements with selected fluorinated substituents; it does not imply that every additional fluorine or ring helps. The O–Cl-bearing seed-2 maximum is one accepted high score, not an endorsement of that bond or a complete molecular design.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ff10f4d5e7f3; frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session. The 4,350 purchases include 607 with >=50 heavy atoms and 597 with >50, versus 837/828 in code Parent n-7e9f57600099. One covered objective contributes 519 of the Child >=50 cases, despite compact leaders elsewhere. Only eight purchases meet either <=5 or <=6 atoms, so fragmentation is a small tail here. These are matched-context chemistry descriptions, not component attribution. Sources: policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and its original-input mapping.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-preserving core and linker changes remain unevenly represented; some sessions still substitute large repeated assemblies for compact alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs coherent ring, core and linker alternatives that preserve overall scale and neighboring functional groups without requiring repeated fragment addition. The evidence does not justify a universal size cutoff, a new size reward, or the assertion that larger molecules always score worse.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ff10f4d5e7f3, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session: 760 purchases carry N–halogen bonds, 125 O–halogen bonds and 59 O–O bonds; code Parent n-7e9f57600099 counts are 565, 63 and 175 under the complete matching context. High-score witnesses include N-halogen carboxamides, a peroxide-linked carbonyl group and an O–Cl-bearing compact heterocycle. Carbon-centred two-double-bond matches occur in 276 purchases; the separate 341 sulfur-centred matches are not automatically liabilities. Flags are local graph properties, not measured stability or toxicity. Sources: policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/bond-context-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The accepted output does not reliably retain conventional bond environments while decorating recognizable functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemically typed substitutions and recombinations should be able to preserve intact amide, amine, ether and carbonyl environments while varying adjacent structure. This is a generator expressivity and chemical-coherence gap to test, not a proven benefit of any hard filter or an instruction to insert a particular benchmark motif.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ff10f4d5e7f3, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session: all 4,350 purchases lack formal charges, assigned tetrahedral configurations or specified double-bond geometry, despite 6,666 unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,672 molecules. Ring amines, aminals, fluorinated cages and polyenes are already present. Code Parent n-7e9f57600099 shows the same absence under the complete matching context. This describes realized output, not an inability of SMILES to encode states or an observed score benefit from adding them. Source: policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic and potentially ionizable structures are emitted without explicit stereochemical or charge-state alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to preserve or coherently vary stereochemical and charge-state distinctions created by its edits. A neutral, unspecified molecular graph should not stand in for evidence of one stereoisomer, one solution protonation state or one accessible conformation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ff10f4d5e7f3, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session: 294 structures have a perceived cycle of at most four atoms with every atom marked aromatic, and 373 contain a perceived ring of at least nine atoms. Aromatic atom flags do not establish that every bond or the small cycle itself is aromatic. Actual quoted leaders include a fused four-membered unsaturated carbocycle, a cyclic allene, polyamine cages and heavily condensed heteroaromatic systems. Ring perception and valid valence are not measurements of strain, stability or synthetic accessibility; unusual cycles are not intrinsically impossible. Sources: policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/bond-context-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Complex ring connectivity is generated without accompanying evidence that its stereochemical and geometric constraints can be realized.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Coherent ring-size, junction, unsaturation and stereochemical transformations would let the generator explore new cores with a clearer path to chemical realization. This does not imply a blanket prohibition on fused, bridged or large rings, nor does it identify a current algorithm component as the cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-ff10f4d5e7f3, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten, 290 accepted optimizer purchases per session: 1,969 typed and 1,240 generic Murcko scaffolds overall, yet two separate task-level top-87 sets contain only four and seven generic scaffolds. Other leading sets retain more topology, so this is local concentration, not universal collapse. Fragment-excluded within-batch count Tanimoto is 0.749127 versus 0.743529 in code Parent n-7e9f57600099 under the complete matching context, with no cross-session pairs. Exact-score peripheral-substitution ties are visible. These associated chemical patterns do not establish component mediation or a diversity benefit. Source: policy/scratch/r0072-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad aggregate scaffold variety does not consistently supply distinct compact alternatives among the highest-scoring local analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing breadth is access to coherent alternative cores and linker/ring arrangements that retain useful neighboring groups, beyond peripheral atom swaps. Such alternatives must remain task-agnostic; their value has to be learned from genuine accepted feedback rather than assumed from a scaffold-count reward.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
